title: feat(plugin-audit): an @mention also reaches the mentioned person by e-mail (default on, mutable per person)
body:

_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwBQ3DFv6XZAspQRYGQoEWhr8)_
Fixes #34729

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

repo:objectstack#3 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufzgNCAXyGfBQFZBwixH

## 维护者速读

1. **改了什么**：被 @ 的人现在除了站内铃铛，还会收到一封邮件（默认开启）。邮件标题是「某某提到了你」，正文是评论片段，最后一行是跳到那条记录的链接。每个人可以在通知偏好里把 @ 邮件单独关掉，站内信照常。
2. **为什么改**：以前 @ 只进站内铃铛。人不在线就一直看不到。
3. **风险与回滚**：邮件量会增加。同一个人在同一个 10 分钟窗口内（按整点 :00、:10、… 对齐）只发一封 @ 邮件，窗口里后面的 @ 只进站内信。所以每人每天最多 144 封 @ 邮件，托管环境的平台代发每日上限按这个估算。回滚就是 revert 本 PR，审批和其他通知不受影响。
4. **先看**：`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts`（@ 写入器里新增的第二次 emit，只走 email，按窗口去重），`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/mention-email.ts`（窗口、去重键、11 种语言的邮件模板），`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-plugin.ts`（启动时注册模板，链接用 auth 服务的 `getConsoleUrl` 拼）。
5. **两分钟验证**：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit exec vitest run src/mention-email.integration.test.ts`，预期 5 个用例全绿：默认收到站内信加 1 封邮件；简体中文用户收到中文标题和中文链接行；关掉邮件后只有站内信；10 分钟内连续 @ 三次只有 1 封邮件，下一个窗口再发 1 封；同一条评论 @ 两个人，两人各收 1 封。
6. **需要你做的**：无，席位落地。

## What changes

- **The mention writer sends a second `collab.mention` emit for the e-mail** (`audit-writers.ts`). The inbox emit is byte-for-byte what it was: no `channels`, deduplicated per comment and person. The new emit names `channels: ['email']` and carries `payload.mentionUrl`. It is deduplicated per organization, person and 10-minute window (`mentionEmailDedupKey`). Both go through `messaging.emit`, so ADR-0030 Decision §5 (single ingress, no side send) holds.
- **Muting per person** is the existing preference filter. Both emits name the topic `collab.mention`, so a `sys_notification_preference` row `(user, collab.mention, email, enabled: false)` mutes the e-mail and keeps the inbox notice. `(user, *, email)` mutes all e-mail. The e-mail is on by default because the matrix is on by default.
- **The burst window is 10 minutes**, clock-aligned (UTC epoch buckets `:00`, `:10`, …), per organization and person. The first mention of a person in a window sends the e-mail. Later mentions in that window go to the inbox only. Bound: one mention e-mail per person per window, at most two in any ten minutes when a burst crosses a window edge, and at most 144 a day.
- **The hosted daily mail cap.** On hosted deployments platform-sent mail has a daily cap (triage 6944467388). The window above is what keeps mention e-mail inside that cap: worst case 144 per person per day, typically one per active thread burst.
- **The e-mail text** (`mention-email.ts`). One code-declared template per catalog locale (the 11 the plugin-audit message catalog carries, the same set the approval e-mail covers), registered by `AuditPlugin` at kernel:ready through `MessagingService.registerBuiltinTemplates`. An organization's own `sys_notification_template` row overrides it. Subject: the notification title, already in the reader's language (`resolveWriteLocale`). Body: the comment preview (240 chars, as the inbox), then one localized line that opens the record. Plain text.
- **The deep link** is the inbox notice's own `/{object}/{id}`, made absolute by the auth service's `getConsoleUrl` (`${origin}${uiBasePath}${path}`, the one composer of Console page links in mail). The Console's catch-all hosts an app-relative path into the reader's app and redirects `/{object}/{id}` to the record page. The link carries no token. Without an auth service the link stays relative. A comment whose thread names no record sends no e-mail.
- **Why two emits and not `['inbox','email']` in one, as approvals do.** The burst bound needs a durable, cluster-safe per-window claim. The only one messaging already has is the event `dedup_key` (unique on `sys_notification`, a repeat emit is a no-op). The inbox has to stay one notice per comment, and the e-mail one per window. That is two keys, and one event holds one key. So the e-mail is its own emit. I checked whether the digest machinery could carry the window: it can only be armed from a stored preference row (`digest` daily/weekly), so a producer cannot ask for it without a new `EmitInput` member. A digest also renders a bullet list of titles, so the snippet and the link would be lost. No service-messaging code changed.

## Tests

- `mention-email.integration.test.ts` (new): real `ObjectQL` over `SqliteWasmDriver`, the real mention writer firing from `afterInsert` on `sys_comment`, and the real `MessagingServicePlugin` with its durable outbox, dispatcher, preference filter and template tier. A recording `email` transport stands in for mail. Five cases: default (inbox `success` + one e-mail; subject `Alice mentioned you`; text is the preview plus `Open the comment:` and the absolute record link); zh-CN (a reader whose `sys_user.locale` is `zh-CN` gets subject `Alice 提到了你` and the `查看评论：` link line); muted (inbox only for the muted person, both channels for an unmuted co-recipient); burst (three mentions inside one window give three inbox notices and one e-mail; the next window sends one more); per person (two people in one burst get one e-mail each).
- `mention-email.test.ts` (new): templates cover exactly the catalog locales, with holes `body` and `mentionUrl` only; window math (same bucket, next bucket, per person, per organization); `AuditPlugin` registers the templates and composes the link through `auth.getConsoleUrl`; no auth service means no absolute link; a refused registration warns once and the writers still install.
- Existing mention tests that count emits by topic now read the inbox notice (`!e.channels`). `audit-hook-object-scope.test.ts` asserts both emits.
- **The recipient gate covers the e-mail too** (L1-d M1). In `mention-recipient-gate.integration.test.ts`, every helper that reads the emits (`comment`, `postTold`, `editTold`, and the two direct reads) goes through `mentionEmits`. It asserts that the `['email']` emits went to exactly the people the inbox emits went to, in the same order, and that no third shape exists. A new case shows that a withheld user (BOB, by id and by e-mail) gets neither emit, and the reader (CAROL) gets both, the e-mail carrying the preview and the record link. The pins that say nothing may be emitted read the whole `collab.mention` topic again: the nested-hook pin there, and the no-gate and failing-gate pins in `audit-writers.test.ts`. The admitted-recipients pin in `audit-writers.test.ts` also asserts the e-mail audience.
- **CONTROL, approvals unchanged:** `plugin-approvals` `approval-email-notification.integration.test.ts` and `approval-email-templates.test.ts` are green unchanged (8/8). No messaging code changed.

## Acceptance notes

- **Surface beyond the claim's file list:** `audit-plugin.ts` (composition: template registration and the auth link composer, mirroring `approvals-plugin.ts`), plus `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` (+3 lines) and `vitest.config.ts`. Those three add `@objectstack/service-messaging` as a devDependency, aliased to source, so the e-mail is tested through the real messaging service. No cycle: service-messaging depends on nothing in plugin-audit.
- **Public surface:** `installAuditWriters` options gain one optional member, `getConsoleUrl`. That options type is not exported by name, and `AuditPluginOptions` is unchanged. The local structural `MessagingEmitSurface` gains `channels` and an optional `registerBuiltinTemplates`, both of which `MessagingService` already implements. No spec, no `EmitInput` and no messaging change, so `Clause-②: no` as the claim declares.
- **Read-only observation, not filed:** the approval e-mail's link is `${publicBaseUrl}/system/approvals?request=ID`, with no `/_console` mount, while `os serve` serves the Console under `/_console/*` and redirects only `/`. Read from source only, with no public-door measurement, so it is noted here and not filed.
- An e-mail emit for a person who muted it still writes its `sys_notification` event row (the filter runs after the event write), and it spends that window's key. This is harmless: the person stays muted.
